q: What is the maximum number of instances that can be attached to a single EBS volume using Multi-Attach?

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is not 4 instances.
exp.b: Incorrect. The limit is not 8 instances.
exp.c: Correct. Multi-Attach allows up to 16 EC2 instances to be attached to a single io1/io2 EBS volume simultaneously.
exp.d: Incorrect. The limit is 16, not 32.

q: What is the minimum volume size for an EBS gp2/gp3 volume?

exp.a: Correct. The minimum size for gp2 and gp3 volumes is 1 GiB.
exp.b: Incorrect. 4 GiB is not the minimum size for gp2/gp3.
exp.c: Incorrect. 8 GiB is not the minimum; it is 1 GiB.
exp.d: Incorrect. 10 GiB is not the minimum size.

q: What is the maximum volume size for an EBS gp2/gp3 volume?

exp.a: Incorrect. 1 TiB is not the maximum for gp2/gp3.
exp.b: Incorrect. 4 TiB is not the maximum for gp2/gp3.
exp.c: Correct. The maximum size for gp2 and gp3 volumes is 16 TiB.
exp.d: Incorrect. 64 TiB exceeds the maximum EBS volume size.

q: What is the maximum IOPS for a gp2 EBS volume?

exp.a: Incorrect. 3,000 IOPS is the baseline/burst for small gp2 volumes, not the maximum.
exp.b: Incorrect. 10,000 IOPS is not the maximum for gp2.
exp.c: Correct. gp2 volumes can deliver a maximum of 16,000 IOPS.
exp.d: Incorrect. 64,000 IOPS is the maximum for io1/io2 volumes, not gp2.

q: What is the maximum IOPS for a gp3 EBS volume?

exp.a: Incorrect. 3,000 IOPS is the baseline for gp3, not the maximum.
exp.b: Correct. gp3 volumes can be provisioned up to a maximum of 16,000 IOPS.
exp.c: Incorrect. 32,000 IOPS exceeds the gp3 maximum.
exp.d: Incorrect. 64,000 IOPS is the maximum for io1/io2, not gp3.

q: What is the baseline IOPS for a gp3 volume?

exp.a: Incorrect. The baseline is not 1,000 IOPS for gp3.
exp.b: Correct. gp3 volumes provide a baseline of 3,000 IOPS regardless of volume size.
exp.c: Incorrect. 5,000 IOPS is not the gp3 baseline.
exp.d: Incorrect. 10,000 IOPS is not the baseline for gp3.

q: What is the baseline throughput for a gp3 volume?

exp.a: Incorrect. 64 MiB/s is not the baseline throughput for gp3.
exp.b: Correct. gp3 volumes provide a baseline throughput of 125 MiB/s.
exp.c: Incorrect. 250 MiB/s is not the baseline; gp3 can be provisioned up to 1,000 MiB/s.
exp.d: Incorrect. 500 MiB/s is above the baseline for gp3.

q: What is the maximum throughput for a gp3 volume?

exp.a: Incorrect. 250 MiB/s is the maximum throughput for gp2, not gp3.
exp.b: Incorrect. 500 MiB/s is the maximum throughput for st1, not gp3.
exp.c: Correct. gp3 volumes can be provisioned up to 1,000 MiB/s throughput.
exp.d: Incorrect. 2,000 MiB/s exceeds the gp3 maximum throughput.

q: How does gp2 calculate its IOPS performance?

opts.b: 3 IOPS per GiB with a minimum burst of 3,000 IOPS

exp.a: Incorrect. IOPS scales with volume size in gp2, it is not always fixed at 3,000.
exp.b: Correct. gp2 provides 3 IOPS per GiB of volume size, with a burst capability of up to 3,000 IOPS for volumes under 1,000 GiB.
exp.c: Incorrect. 10 IOPS per GiB is not the gp2 formula.
exp.d: Incorrect. 50 IOPS per GiB applies to io1/io2 ratio, not gp2.

q: What is the maximum IOPS for an io1 EBS volume?

exp.a: Incorrect. 16,000 IOPS is the max for gp2/gp3.
exp.b: Incorrect. 32,000 IOPS is not the max for io1.
exp.c: Correct. io1 volumes support a maximum of 64,000 IOPS.
exp.d: Incorrect. 256,000 IOPS is the max for io2 Block Express, not standard io1.

q: What is the maximum IOPS for an io2 Block Express EBS volume?

exp.a: Incorrect. 64,000 IOPS is the max for standard io1/io2.
exp.b: Incorrect. 128,000 is not the correct maximum for io2 Block Express.
exp.c: Correct. io2 Block Express supports up to 256,000 IOPS.
exp.d: Incorrect. 500,000 IOPS exceeds the io2 Block Express maximum.

q: What is the IOPS-to-GiB ratio for io1 volumes?

exp.a: Incorrect. 3 IOPS per GiB applies to gp2 volumes.
exp.b: Incorrect. 10 IOPS per GiB is not the io1 ratio.
exp.c: Correct. io1 volumes support up to 50 IOPS per GiB of provisioned storage.
exp.d: Incorrect. 100 IOPS per GiB is not the correct ratio for io1.

q: What is the IOPS-to-GiB ratio for io2 Block Express volumes?

exp.a: Incorrect. 50 IOPS per GiB applies to io1.
exp.b: Incorrect. 100 IOPS per GiB is not the ratio for io2 Block Express.
exp.c: Incorrect. 500 IOPS per GiB is not the correct ratio.
exp.d: Correct. io2 Block Express supports up to 1,000 IOPS per GiB.

q: What is the maximum volume size for io2 Block Express?

exp.a: Incorrect. 16 TiB is the max for standard EBS volumes like gp2/gp3/io1.
exp.b: Incorrect. 32 TiB is not the max for io2 Block Express.
exp.c: Correct. io2 Block Express volumes can be up to 64 TiB in size.
exp.d: Incorrect. 128 TiB exceeds the maximum for io2 Block Express.

q: What is the maximum throughput for an st1 (Throughput Optimized HDD) volume?

exp.a: Incorrect. 250 MiB/s is the max throughput for sc1 and gp2.
exp.b: Correct. st1 volumes can achieve a maximum throughput of 500 MiB/s.
exp.c: Incorrect. 1,000 MiB/s is the max throughput for gp3.
exp.d: Incorrect. 125 MiB/s is the baseline throughput for gp3.

q: What is the maximum throughput for an sc1 (Cold HDD) volume?

exp.a: Incorrect. 125 MiB/s is not the max throughput for sc1.
exp.b: Correct. sc1 volumes can achieve a maximum throughput of 250 MiB/s.
exp.c: Incorrect. 500 MiB/s is the max throughput for st1.
exp.d: Incorrect. 40 MiB/s is too low for sc1 max throughput.

q: What is the maximum IOPS for an st1 volume?

exp.a: Incorrect. 250 IOPS is the max for sc1, not st1.
exp.b: Correct. st1 volumes support a maximum of 500 IOPS.
exp.c: Incorrect. 1,000 IOPS exceeds st1 capability.
exp.d: Incorrect. 16,000 IOPS is the max for gp2/gp3, not st1.

q: What is the maximum IOPS for an sc1 volume?

exp.a: Incorrect. 100 IOPS is not the max for sc1.
exp.b: Correct. sc1 volumes support a maximum of 250 IOPS.
exp.c: Incorrect. 500 IOPS is the max for st1, not sc1.
exp.d: Incorrect. 1,000 IOPS far exceeds sc1 capability.

q: What is the minimum size for st1 and sc1 volumes?

exp.a: Incorrect. 1 GiB is the minimum for gp2/gp3, not st1/sc1.
exp.b: Correct. Both st1 and sc1 volumes have a minimum size of 125 GiB.
exp.c: Incorrect. 500 GiB is not the minimum for st1/sc1.
exp.d: Incorrect. 1,000 GiB is not the minimum for these volume types.

q: What retention period can you set for the EBS Recycle Bin?

exp.a: Correct. You can set a retention period from 1 day to 1 year (365 days) for the EBS Recycle Bin.
exp.b: Incorrect. 7 days is not the only option.
exp.c: Incorrect. 30 days is not the only option.
exp.d: Incorrect. There is a maximum retention of 1 year.

q: What is the durability of EBS volumes?

exp.a: Incorrect. This is incomplete.
exp.b: Correct. Standard EBS volumes (gp2/gp3/st1/sc1) offer 99.8%-99.9% durability, while io1/io2 offer 99.999% durability.
exp.c: Incorrect. Durability varies by volume type.
exp.d: Incorrect. No storage service guarantees 100% durability.

q: What is the SLA availability for EBS volumes?

exp.a: Incorrect. 99.0% is too low for EBS SLA.
exp.b: Incorrect. 99.9% is lower than the actual EBS SLA.
exp.c: Correct. EBS provides an SLA of 99.99% availability.
exp.d: Incorrect. 99.999% is the durability for io1/io2, not the availability SLA.

q: How many EBS volumes can you attach to a single EC2 instance (approximate maximum)?

exp.a: Incorrect. You can attach more than 5 volumes.
exp.b: Incorrect. The limit is higher than 10.
exp.c: Correct. You can typically attach up to 28 EBS volumes to a single EC2 instance (limit varies by instance type, with some Nitro instances supporting more).
exp.d: Incorrect. 128 is too high for standard instances.

q: An application running on EC2 uses a gp2 volume of 200 GiB. What is the baseline IOPS performance of this volume?

exp.a: Incorrect. The formula is 3 IOPS per GiB, not 1 IOPS per GiB.
exp.b: Correct. gp2 provides 3 IOPS per GiB, so 200 GiB × 3 = 600 IOPS baseline. However, it can burst up to 3,000 IOPS.
exp.c: Incorrect. 3,000 IOPS is the burst capability, not the sustained baseline for a 200 GiB volume.
exp.d: Incorrect. The calculation is 200 × 3 = 600 IOPS.

q: A gp2 volume of 200 GiB has a baseline of 600 IOPS. What burst IOPS can it achieve?

exp.a: Incorrect. 600 IOPS is the baseline, not the burst.
exp.b: Incorrect. 1,800 IOPS is not the burst limit.
exp.c: Correct. All gp2 volumes below 1,000 GiB can burst up to 3,000 IOPS regardless of their baseline.
exp.d: Incorrect. 16,000 IOPS is the maximum for gp2 volumes at 5,334 GiB or larger.

q: At what size does a gp2 volume reach its maximum IOPS of 16,000 without needing burst credits?

exp.a: Incorrect. 1,000 GiB × 3 = 3,000 IOPS, not 16,000.
exp.b: Incorrect. 3,000 GiB × 3 = 9,000 IOPS, not 16,000.
exp.c: Correct. 16,000 IOPS ÷ 3 IOPS per GiB = 5,334 GiB. At this size, the baseline equals the maximum.
exp.d: Incorrect. 16,000 GiB would still provide 16,000 IOPS (the max), but 5,334 GiB is the point where baseline reaches max.

q: An EBS io1 volume of 100 GiB is provisioned. What is the maximum IOPS that can be provisioned for this volume?

exp.a: Incorrect. The maximum is calculated as 50 IOPS × GiB size.
exp.b: Correct. io1 supports up to 50 IOPS per GiB, so 100 GiB × 50 = 5,000 IOPS maximum for this volume size.
exp.c: Incorrect. 10,000 IOPS would require at least 200 GiB (200 × 50 = 10,000).
exp.d: Incorrect. 64,000 IOPS is the absolute max for io1, but volume size limits it to 5,000 for 100 GiB.

q: What minimum volume size is needed for an io1 volume to achieve its maximum of 64,000 IOPS?

exp.a: Incorrect. 640 × 50 = 32,000 IOPS, not 64,000.
exp.b: Correct. 64,000 IOPS ÷ 50 IOPS per GiB = 1,280 GiB minimum volume size needed.
exp.c: Incorrect. 3,200 GiB × 50 = 160,000, which exceeds the maximum anyway (capped at 64,000).
exp.d: Incorrect. 6,400 GiB is more than needed.

q: A snapshot was taken of a 500 GiB EBS volume that only has 100 GiB of data. How much storage does the first snapshot approximately consume?

exp.a: Incorrect. Snapshots only store used blocks, not the full allocated volume size.
exp.b: Correct. The first snapshot stores only the blocks that contain data, approximately 100 GiB in this case.
exp.c: Incorrect. It does not store half the volume size.
exp.d: Incorrect. The first snapshot stores all used blocks, approximately 100 GiB.

q: After the initial 100 GiB snapshot, 20 GiB of data is modified. How much additional storage does the second snapshot consume?

exp.a: Incorrect. The second snapshot only stores changed blocks.
exp.b: Incorrect. The second snapshot does not store all data again.
exp.c: Correct. EBS snapshots are incremental, so the second snapshot only stores the 20 GiB of changed blocks.
exp.d: Incorrect. Snapshots are incremental, not full copies.

q: What is the maximum throughput of an io2 Block Express volume?

exp.a: Incorrect. 1,000 MiB/s is the max for gp3 and standard io1/io2.
exp.b: Incorrect. 2,000 MiB/s is not the max for io2 Block Express.
exp.c: Correct. io2 Block Express supports up to 4,000 MiB/s throughput.
exp.d: Incorrect. 10,000 MiB/s exceeds io2 Block Express capabilities.

q: A company uses RAID 0 striping with four 4 TiB gp3 volumes each provisioned at 16,000 IOPS. What is the aggregate IOPS of the RAID 0 array?

exp.a: Incorrect. RAID 0 adds the IOPS of all volumes.
exp.b: Incorrect. 32,000 would be two volumes.
exp.c: Incorrect. 48,000 would be three volumes.
exp.d: Correct. RAID 0 stripes data across all volumes, so aggregate IOPS = 4 × 16,000 = 64,000 IOPS.

q: What is the maximum number of EBS snapshots you can have per AWS account per region?

opts.d: Unlimited (soft limit of 100,000 with possible increase)

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is higher than 1,000.
exp.b: Incorrect. The limit is higher than 10,000.
exp.c: Correct. The default limit is 100,000 EBS snapshots per account per region.
exp.d: Incorrect. While you can request an increase, the default is 100,000, not unlimited.

q: What is the maximum number of EBS volumes per account per region (default)?

exp.a: Incorrect. The default limit is higher than 500.
exp.b: Correct. The default limit is 5,000 EBS volumes per account per region (can be increased by request).
exp.c: Incorrect. 10,000 is not the default limit for volumes.
exp.d: Incorrect. 50,000 far exceeds the default limit.

q: You need to ensure that your EBS-backed EC2 instance can handle a sudden spike of I/O during business hours. The volume is gp2 with 100 GiB. What is the burst duration approximately?

opts.b: Approximately 30 minutes at 3,000 IOPS with a full credit balance

exp.a: Incorrect. Burst is not indefinite; it depends on credit balance.
exp.b: Correct. A 100 GiB gp2 volume has a 300 IOPS baseline and 5.4 million burst credits. At 3,000 IOPS burst, credits deplete in approximately 5,400,000 / (3,000 - 300) = ~2,000 seconds ≈ 33 minutes.
exp.c: Incorrect. 60 minutes would require more credits than available.
exp.d: Incorrect. 5 minutes is too short for a full credit balance.

q: What is the maximum throughput for a standard io1/io2 volume (non-Block Express)?

exp.a: Incorrect. 250 MiB/s is the max throughput for gp2 and sc1.
exp.b: Incorrect. 500 MiB/s is the max for st1.
exp.c: Correct. Standard io1/io2 volumes support up to 1,000 MiB/s throughput.
exp.d: Incorrect. 4,000 MiB/s is the max for io2 Block Express.

q: What is the io2 standard (non-Block Express) IOPS-to-GiB ratio?

exp.a: Incorrect. 50 IOPS per GiB is the ratio for io1.
exp.b: Incorrect. 100 IOPS per GiB is not the io2 ratio.
exp.c: Correct. Standard io2 provides up to 500 IOPS per GiB (compared to 50 for io1).
exp.d: Incorrect. 1,000 IOPS per GiB is the ratio for io2 Block Express.

q: What is the maximum size of an I/O operation for SSD-based EBS volumes (gp2, gp3, io1, io2)?

exp.a: Incorrect. 16 KiB is the I/O size counted as one IOPS for SSD volumes.
exp.b: Incorrect. 64 KiB is not the maximum I/O size for SSD volumes.
exp.c: Correct. SSD-based EBS volumes support a maximum I/O size of 256 KiB. Each 16 KiB counts as one IOPS.
exp.d: Incorrect. 1 MiB is the maximum I/O size for HDD volumes, not SSD.

q: What is the maximum size of an I/O operation for HDD-based EBS volumes (st1, sc1)?

exp.a: Incorrect. 16 KiB is too small for HDD maximum I/O.
exp.b: Incorrect. 256 KiB is the max for SSD volumes.
exp.c: Incorrect. 512 KiB is not the correct maximum for HDD volumes.
exp.d: Correct. HDD-based EBS volumes (st1, sc1) support a maximum I/O size of 1 MiB.

q: An application writes 256 KiB I/O operations to a gp3 volume. How many IOPS does each write consume?

exp.a: Incorrect. For SSD volumes, 1 IOPS = 16 KiB.
exp.b: Incorrect. 4 IOPS would be 64 KiB.
exp.c: Correct. For SSD volumes, each 16 KiB counts as 1 IOPS. A 256 KiB operation = 256 / 16 = 16 IOPS.
exp.d: Incorrect. 256 IOPS is too high; the calculation is 256 KiB / 16 KiB = 16.

q: A 2 TiB st1 volume is created. What is its baseline throughput?

exp.a: Incorrect. 40 MiB/s is the baseline per TiB, so 1 TiB would get 40 MiB/s.
exp.b: Correct. Baseline = 40 MiB/s × 2 TiB = 80 MiB/s.
exp.c: Incorrect. 250 MiB/s per TiB is the burst rate, not baseline.
exp.d: Incorrect. 500 MiB/s is the maximum burst throughput regardless of size.

q: A developer creates an io2 volume of 200 GiB. What is the maximum IOPS they can provision using the standard io2 (non-Block Express) ratio?

exp.a: Incorrect. With 500 IOPS/GiB ratio: 200 × 500 = 100,000. But the maximum cap for standard io2 is 64,000 IOPS.
exp.b: Correct. While 200 GiB × 500 IOPS/GiB = 100,000, the standard io2 volume cap is 64,000 IOPS, so the maximum is 64,000 IOPS.
exp.c: Incorrect. The ratio allows 100,000 but the volume type cap is 64,000 for standard io2.
exp.d: Incorrect. 200,000 exceeds all standard io2 limits.

q: What is the throughput calculation for st1 volumes?

opts.b: 40 MiB/s per TiB baseline, bursting to 250 MiB/s per TiB

exp.a: Incorrect. That formula is for gp2 IOPS.
exp.b: Correct. st1 provides 40 MiB/s per TiB as baseline throughput, with burst capability up to 250 MiB/s per TiB, capped at 500 MiB/s maximum.
exp.c: Incorrect. 500 MiB/s is the maximum, not a flat rate for all sizes.
exp.d: Incorrect. 125 MiB/s is the gp3 baseline, not st1.

q: What is the throughput calculation for sc1 volumes?

opts.a: 12 MiB/s per TiB baseline, bursting to 80 MiB/s per TiB
opts.b: 40 MiB/s per TiB baseline, bursting to 250 MiB/s per TiB

exp.a: Correct. sc1 provides 12 MiB/s per TiB baseline throughput, bursting to 80 MiB/s per TiB, capped at 250 MiB/s maximum.
exp.b: Incorrect. This is the formula for st1, not sc1.
exp.c: Incorrect. 125 MiB/s is the gp3 baseline.
exp.d: Incorrect. 500 MiB/s is the st1 maximum throughput.
